A SuperStation One is in hand, so rung 6 is unblocked and v2.7.0 — the MiSTer-devel submission — is reachable for the first time in eight releases. This is the pre-flight, and its subject is that bring-up should start from a base whose records are true.

Almost everything below was found by a check that already existed and had never been run, or by a tool that only speaks when asked. **The emulation core is unchanged**, so AccuracyCoin **144/144** and nestest 0-diff hold by construction, and were re-run anyway.

The co-simulation ladder on the final RTL is **152 passed, 0 failed, 1 expected failure** — the expected one being new, deliberate, and graded both ways; see below.

## Battery saves exist

`T-MISTER-SAVE` had been open since v2.6.12 under the note *"Scheduled for v2.6.13"*. It never landed, so `rtl/emu.sv` tied `sd_lba`, `sd_rd`, `sd_wr` and `sd_buff_din` to constants and **every MMC1 or MMC3 game with a battery lost its save at power-off** — *Zelda*, *Final Fantasy*, *Kirby's Adventure*, *Crystalis* — with nothing in the OSD to say so. It is the one board item with a user-visible data-loss cost.

**The plan's protocol was wrong, and the framework settled it.** The plan said to use `ioctl_upload_req`/`ioctl_din` and explicitly not `sd_*`. `Main_MiSTer/user_io.cpp:948-955` says otherwise: an **`S`** after the `F` in a `CONF_STR` file entry sets `opensave`, which calls `FileGenerateSavePath()` then `user_io_file_mount(path, 0, 1)`. The save therefore arrives as **vdisk 0 over `sd_*`**, and that one letter is what buys `<rom>.sav` naming and load-on-ROM-load. `F1,NES;` becomes `FS1,NES;`.

The mechanism is `rtl/save_ctl.sv`, its own module because `rtl/emu.sv` is in no testbench — which is how v2.6.12 shipped a cartridge hard-wired to mapper 0 with 142 gates green. The policy (when to save: the rising edge of `OSD_STATUS`) stays in `emu.sv`, the only file that can see it. Nine cases in `make -C tb save-gate`, five of them **refusals** — a clean cartridge, a zero-length file, a read-only mount, no battery, no vdisk — which matter more than the round trip: without them a controller that saves unconditionally passes and rewrites `<rom>.sav` on every OSD visit.

**Two further defects came out of review, and both were reachable.** There was no exit from `S_SAVE` but completion, and `rst_n` is `pll_locked`, which does not drop on a ROM load — so a host that stopped answering left the controller asserting `busy` forever *with the dirty flag already cleared*, since the clear is at the start by design so a CPU write landing mid-save leaves it raised. And the `S_LOAD`/`S_SAVE` arm did not look at `img_mounted` **at all**, so a cartridge inserted during a transfer had its mount dropped and its save never read for the rest of the session. A per-block watchdog ends an abandoned transfer, `save_failed` holds `save_pending` high for a retry, and a mount is captured in every state and **outranks** a pending save.

The hardware half — a save surviving a power cycle — is v2.7.0.

## `prg_ram` was 8 KiB of flip-flops, and the block count was never the variable

Adding the second port made Quartus refuse the design outright:

```text
Error (170011): Design contains 151605 blocks of type combinational node.
However, the device contains only 83820 blocks.
```

The obvious fix made it **worse** — merging both ports into one `always_ff` gave 159,216 blocks and **217 %** ALM utilisation. Each version carried a confident comment, and the two contradicted each other about whether a dual-port memory is one block or two. Neither was the variable.

The fitter named the real shape in a table nobody reads: **8192 multiplexers, 8 bits wide, 3:1** — hold, port-A data, port-B data, which is a two-write-port register file described exactly — while `prg_ram` was simply **absent** from the Analysis & Synthesis RAM Summary that listed `wram`, `prg` and `chr`.

**What decides it is the read-during-write style.** Each port's read must sit in the `else` branch of that port's own write, so the port reads back what it just wrote, because that is what an M10K port physically does. A port that returns the OLD value on a write cycle is not a mode the hardware has, so Quartus cannot map it and builds logic instead. `wram.sv` reads unconditionally and infers fine *because it has one port*: a single-port RAM does have a read-old mode.

With Intel's template: `OPERATION_MODE set to BIDIR_DUAL_PORT`, 8192 × 8, zero 3:1 multiplexers.

**Nothing but the fitter could have found it.** Verilator accepts all three forms and the save gate passed on both broken ones — correct behaviour, unfittable hardware — and `check_rtl_subset.py` passed on all three, because it checks policy rather than inference. `docs/rtl-subset-policy.md` gains the two-port rule beside the single-port one, with the three ways to tell before a fit fails and the note that `quartus_map` answers all three in ~5 minutes against ~25 for a full compile.

## Eighteen gates could be silenced by a stray file

A target absent from `.PHONY` is satisfied by a **file** of that name: make prints "up to date", runs nothing, exits 0 — and `regress.sh` reads exit 0 as **PASS**. Demonstrated in a throwaway whose `save-gate` recipe exits 1: exit 2 with no such file, exit 0 after `touch save-gate`. So a stray file turns a failing gate into a passing one with no output saying so.

Review named two. An audit found **eighteen**, sixteen of them invoked by `regress.sh`. All declared, and `tb/check_phony.py` + `make -C tb phony-audit` keep it that way in CI, with a five-case self-test and a mutation that fails it by name.

## A permanently red gate destroys the tally it sits in

The CHR-during-rendering gate this release adds is **RED**, deliberately: `docs/STATUS.md` claimed v2.6.20's CHR-RAM gate "closes the coverage the retrospective audit named", and it does not — the audit named writes **while rendering is enabled**, and PROGRAM53 writes with `PPUMASK = 0`. PROGRAM54 writes mid-frame, and **32,861 of 61,440 pixels differ** with `chr_wr` asserted 4,389 times. The obvious fix — pointing `chr_wr_addr` at `v_addr` — recovers only **715** of them, so there is at least one more mechanism. Not landed, because an unverified RTL change would also force a full seed re-sweep.

Registered as an ordinary gate it would have made the suite report "N passed, 1 failed" every release, and the next genuinely new failure would print the identical line. `run_xfail` grades it **both ways**: failing is expected and reported as XFAIL; **passing is a hard failure**, because that means the divergence closed and the record is now wrong. `tb/check_xfail.sh` extracts the real functions out of `regress.sh` rather than restating them, and demonstrates all four cases.

## The deploy loop the runbook prescribed, and two defects in its own spec

`docs/HARDWARE_TESTING.md` named `make deploy` / `mgl` / `battery` and `tools/gen_mgl.sh` / `tools/run_battery.sh`. There was no root `Makefile` and no `tools/` directory, which is the prerequisite for Tiers 1-4 — so its absence was the reason none of §5 had ever been executed. Building it found the spec wrong twice: the prescribed MGL `index` default is `0` while `emu.sv` gates on `1`, so every ROM would have gone to a slot nothing decodes (a black screen, no error, an entire battery reporting nothing), and the corpus path named `games/NES`, the stock core's directory.

Review then found more in what was built: `deploy`'s prerequisites are unordered, so `make -j` could push before the build and load before the push; the battery's provenance row took the newest file in `releases/`, which `make deploy` never writes; and both OSD commands carried `|| true`, contradicting the fail-closed contract in the file's own header. The row now carries `rbf_md5` read **off the board**, and a freshness marker means a stale `.sav` reports `needs-capture` — "I could not look" must not wear the shape of "it passed".

## A guard that would have fired on success

`contribution_checklist_audit.rs` asserted `unticked > 0`, reasoning *"rung 6 needs hardware nobody here has"*. A board is now attached, so that sentence is false — and the assertion would have turned **v2.7.0's milestone into a red test** the moment the list completed.

What replaces it is narrower and survives the submission: three of the thirty boxes can never be evidence *about the core* — "Await review" and "Add to the Cores list" are other people's actions, and the DECIDED "publishable on its own terms" box can never fail. Review then caught that the replacement passed **vacuously** if a protected item were renamed away, the same shape as the guard it replaced; existence is asserted first now.

## A suite map that would have built the wrong test

`build_sub_test_rom.py` carried a hand-written map of twenty suites with `PowerOnState` at 14. Upstream's `TableTable` at `46199ae4` has **twenty-two**, `CPUBehavior2` at 14 and `PPUMisc` at 19. A rebuild driven by it **enters the wrong suite and writes a plausible byte for a test nobody asked for**, which is the worst failure available here because it looks like a result. Of its four recorded targets, `Implied Dummy Reads: suite=19` was wrong — it is suite **14**.

`derive_indices.py` replaces it, reading `TableTable` and each suite's own `table` lines out of the assembly. Three things then went wrong in the replacement itself, and all three are the reason it is worth describing:

- it emitted **145 rows for a 149-entry catalog** and said nothing. All five `Suite_PowerOnState` tests name `result_DrawTest`, and upstream's own comment says what that is — `$03FF ; page 3 omits the test from the all-test-result-table` — so it is a **sentinel meaning "this test has no result byte"**, not a location, and keying a map by it kept only the last. Rows are a flat list with a `has_result` column now, and the tool **exits** rather than emit a short catalog;
- it **validated nothing by default**, while its own docstring said the derivation "is VALIDATED against the two rows that were recorded by hand". True of one invocation, false of the default one. The recorded mappings are read from `BUILD-PROVENANCE.tsv` and checked on every run;
- and its docstring **transcribed the corrected map** three lines below the struck one — the same artifact, correct the day it was written. Gone; the builder now cross-checks `--suite`/`--test`/`--name` against the assembly and refuses a mismatch by name.

A control, because "it builds something" is not "it builds the right thing": the accept path produces a ROM differing from the committed `advanced-sprite-eval-misaligned-oam2-address.nes` in exactly **165 bytes** — the same figure measured independently for the deferred upstream corpus re-sync.

## The bitstream

Ten seeds on this release's RTL, each from a **clean database**, all at one pinned build date, worst across all four corners:

```text
seed | worst setup | worst hold | result
  1  |   +0.307    |   +0.068   | closes
  2  |   +0.233    |   +0.078   | closes
  3  |   -0.180    |   +0.073   | DOES NOT CLOSE
  4  |   +0.443    |   +0.079   | closes
  5  |   +0.259    |   +0.102   | closes  <- published
  6  |   +0.218    |   +0.076   | closes
  7  |   +0.135    |   +0.045   | closes
  8  |   +0.456    |   +0.071   | closes
  9  |   +0.245    |   +0.093   | closes
 10  |   +0.159    |   +0.080   | closes
```

**The pin moves 1 → 5.** Hold binds on every closing seed (0.045-0.102 against setup's 0.135-0.456) and seed 5 takes it outright at +0.102.

**The counterexample is back, which is why v2.6.20's last entry was worth writing.** That release recorded seed 8 failing on v2.6.19's RTL, closing on v2.6.20's, and said the *specific* counterexample was gone while the principle stood — that whether every seed closes is a property of the RTL, re-measured each time, and not a fact about the design. On this RTL **seed 3 does not close**, at −0.180 ns of setup. A different seed, one release later, on a design whose ALM utilisation moved 52 % → 55 %. The principle was right, and would have been unfalsifiable had the previous entry quietly dropped it when its evidence expired.

**And note which seed.** Seed 3 was the pin from v2.6.13 through v2.6.19 and was the worst of v2.6.20's ten. It now fails outright — so a pin carried forward on an older RTL's table would not merely have cost margin, it would have shipped a bitstream that does not meet timing. The sweep is what makes that a non-event rather than a late surprise.

`releases/RustyNES_20260919.rbf` ships on both repositories.

## Also in this release

- **The v2.6.20 coverage claim was retracted in one document of five.** The identical sentence stood in `README.md`, `SUPPORT.md`, `ROADMAP.md` and `VERSION-PLAN.md`; all four now carry the retraction.
- **A lineage marker merged two releases** in `ROADMAP.md`, so v2.6.19 appeared twice and v2.6.18 had none. And in `SUPPORT.md` a `(` opened at the v2.6.17 entry closes **26,396 characters** later, so sixteen releases read as an aside to it — the parentheses *balance*, 13 and 13, so a counting check would have called the file clean. A new gate asserts both properties. Its own threshold was 32 KB on the first try, above the 26 KB defect it was written for, and came back NOT CAUGHT until the mutation ran.
- **A measurement of mine is retracted before it shipped.** The same scan reported a 120,221-character defect in `AGENTS.md`. There is none: it counted parentheses inside code spans, and the "fix" deleted a `)` out of `` `syntax error near unexpected token )` ``. **markdownlint MD038 caught that, not the new test.** With code masked, `AGENTS.md` had two unmatched opening parens and `docs/STATUS.md` one — the real defects, now fixed.
- **The RTL is indented with tabs**, as MiSTer's coding guidelines require and as 30 of the 32 vendored `sys/` files already are. The commit that did it asserted the bitstream was unaffected and said the check "rides the ten-seed sweep this release runs anyway" — **it does not**: a sweep measures slack, not a byte-identical artifact, and other RTL changed in the same release, so there was no valid before/after pair. Prompted by review objecting to the conversion's scope, it was then measured properly — the current RTL re-indented back to spaces across all 22 files, compiled from scratch, bitstream compared: **`d20c6dd3f58c58a13ca84c3b823de2a7` both ways**. Whitespace does not reach the synthesiser, and that is now a hash rather than an argument.

- **A bare `always` reached CI.** Verilator's lint accepts it; `check_rtl_subset.py` forbids it. Two gates over the same files, and only one had been run locally. All eight no-simulator CI steps are now run before pushing.

**No hardware has run any bitstream.** That is v2.7.0.
